Deloitte to refund government over AI errors in A$440,000 report

By Fixture Desk, 7 October 2025

Deloitte Australia has agreed to partially refund the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations after a A$440,000 report commissioned in July 2025 was found to contain fabricated references, including a dozen citations to the work of a professor who does not exist and a misquoted judicial decision.

The department said the firm had used a generative AI model, GPT-4o hosted on Azure OpenAI, to assist with drafting. In a statement the department said: "The substance of the independent review is retained, and there are no changes to the recommendations."

Independent audits of deep-research tools report that between 3% and 13% of cited URLs are hallucinated, and 5–18% of cited URLs do not resolve. Fact-check accuracy fell about 42 per cent on average as tool calls rose from 2 to 150.

Separately, a C$1.6 million health workforce plan in Newfoundland was found to carry at least four citations to non-existent papers. Market analysts estimate the consulting AI segment at US$3.2 billion.
